questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. There are many gadgets that are operated by a remote control and contain a silicon chip.

B. This produces an infra-red beam, made up of electromagnetic waves.

C. When a button is pressed on the remote control, the chip sets off an electronic vibration.

D. The beam carries a coded signal for operating the systems.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 3 i.e. ACBD**

The passage begins with **statement A** which talks about how there are too many gadgets that are operated by remote control, then comes **statement C** which talks about how the remote control functions - once the button is pressed, a chip sets off an electronic vibration, then comes **statement B** which talks about the process further - the vibration causes an infrared beam that is made up of electromagnetic waves and finally comes **statement D**, this talks about how the waves carry coded signals for the operating systems.

**Thus, the correct answer is option 3. **

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select No improvement.**

Amit has __the good command on__ English as he was born and brought up in England.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer is **"a good command over".**
 
• In English, when you want to express proficiency in a language, you use the preposition** "over"** or** "of" after "command".**
 
• So the **phrase should** be "Amit has a good command over English" or "Amit has a good command of English".

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is*: "Amit has a good command over English as he was born and brought up in England."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here is why the other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **"A better command of" - **This would be correct if we were comparing Amit's command of English to someone else's. But the sentence does not make any such comparison.
 
• **"The best command in" -** This is not correct. The phrase is either "command of" or "command over". The word "best" implies comparison, but the sentence does not compare Amit's command of English to anyone else's.

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. It is called the atmosphere.

B. All parts of the earth are surrounded by air.

C. Living beings breathe in and breathe out the air all the time.

D. This process is called respiration.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2 i.e. BACD**

The passage begins with **statement B**, this talks about how all parts of the Earth are surrounded by air, then comes **statement A** which talks about what that air is called - atmosphere. This is followed by **statement C** which talks about how living beings breathe and **statement D** names this process as 'respiration'.

**Thus, the correct answer is option 2. **

questions.question:

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3 i.e. are utilized to the overall**

The sentence refers to the responsibilities of a scientist and how their discoveries and inventions are used. 'Utilized' refers to being used and things are not used to development, they are used for development. Thus,** the preposition 'to' needs to be replaced with 'for**'

**Thus, the correct answer is option 3. **

questions.question:
**Select the passive form of the given sentence.**

People claim to have seen the wild and mad elephant in several cities.

options.text: The wild and mad elephant is being claimed to be seen in several cities.
The wild and mad elephant has been claimed to be seen by the people in several cities.
The wild and mad elephant was claimed to be seen by people in several cities.
The wild and mad elephant is claimed to have been seen in several cities.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 4 i.e. The wild and mad elephant is claimed to have been seen in several cities.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The original sentence is in the active voice, the format for this will be:
 
 
• **Subject + Present tense of the Verb + to have seen + Object**
 
 
 
• This needs to be converted to the passive voice, the format for that will be:
 
 
• **Object + is + Third form of the verb + to have been seen + Subject**
 
 
 
• The wild and mad elephant is claimed to have been seen in several cities.

Thus, the correct answer is** option 4. **

questions.question:
**__Direction__: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given Idiom.**

Hobson's Choice

options.text: To be in an aggressive mood when facing a challenge
To exercise the choice to surrender before the enemy
An apparently free choice where there is no real alternative

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- 'an apparently free choice where there is no real alternative.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's understand the meaning of the given idiom:
 
• **Hobson's choice** means one has to make a choice between what is available or nothing at all. (Hobson's choice का मतलब है कि जो उपलब्ध है या बिल्कुल नहीं के बीच चुनाव करना है।)
 
 
• Example: *This is the dirtiest hotel that I have ever slept in! It is this room or out on the street, it’s **Hobson’s choice.***
 
 
 
• From the meaning and example, we can say the correct answer is 'an apparently free choice where there is no real alternative.'

Thus *option 4 *is the most appropriate answer

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's learn about the origin of the idiom:
 
• This phrase has originated in the **1600s**. A stable manager named **Thomas Hobson** (1544 -1631) would allow people to** rent horses** from him but gave them the choice of** the next one in line or none at all.** (यह वाक्यांश **1600** के दशक में उत्पन्न हुआ है। **थॉमस हॉब्सन **(1544 -1631) नाम का एक घुड़साल प्रबंधक लोगों को उससे घोड़े किराए पर लेने की अनुमति देता था, लेकिन उन्हें अगली पंक्ति में **खड़ा घोड़ा **या कोई भी घोड़ा नहीं का विकल्प देता था।)

He said to me, "What time do the banks open and close?"

He said me what time did the banks open and close.

He wanted to know what time the banks open and close.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 3 i.e. He asked me what time the banks opened and closed.**

The original sentence has a question mark, thus the indirect sentence **should have a verb like 'asked' or 'questioned**', thus option 2 and 4 are incorrect because they **use different verbs**. option 1 cannot be used as reported speech is supposed to have** verbs in the past tense, but option 1 uses the present tense.**

**Thus, the correct answer is option 3. **
